families.label: Direct disjoint leaf union
families.definition: Keep both original overclock roots and union leaves whose semantic targets, class filters, event owners and runtime carriers do not overlap.
families.inclusionRule: No same-target recomposition, replacement-slot forwarding, shared input/state conflict or new object fan-out is required.
families.exclusionRule: A different field name alone is insufficient when both leaves still control the same event, replacement slot or runtime state.
families.semanticGuardrail: Do not deduplicate repeated original triggers merely because their leaf types match; preserve each original trigger boundary.
families.smallestExperiment: Read back both leaf sets and compare each original trigger/result once on host and client.

families.label: Same-target numeric recomposition
families.definition: Replace overlapping, same-target numeric leaves with deterministic pair-specific leaves after applying the accepted unit and utility policy; union all other original leaves.
families.inclusionRule: The target, unit, neutral value and legal arithmetic are sufficiently known for flat, percentage or multi-target recomposition.
families.exclusionRule: Do not multiply quantities with units or guess mixed flat/percentage order, integer rounding or target utility.
families.semanticGuardrail: Numeric merging must not merge event counts, projectiles, impacts, impulses, timers or state transitions.
families.smallestExperiment: Read back the final target value and compare one representative gameplay result against the arithmetic expectation.

families.label: Mixed flat/percent carrier unknown
families.definition: Preserve separately known contributions while the native formula, order, integer conversion or stable carrier for a mixed flat/percentage target remains unproved.
families.inclusionRule: The desired policy is known or bounded, but the engine carrier cannot yet be shown to express it exactly.
families.exclusionRule: Technical uncertainty is not evidence that gameplay redesign is necessary.
families.semanticGuardrail: Do not normalize, cap or discard one contribution to avoid resolving the carrier.
families.smallestExperiment: Probe one final runtime value with asymmetric inputs that distinguish order and rounding.

families.label: Original event/component union
families.definition: Retain exactly one original owner for a hit counter, overheat callback, persistent actor, status route, input event or other component, and union independent leaves around it.
families.inclusionRule: The original component/event already implements the required behavior and no second competing owner is needed.
families.exclusionRule: Do not clone listeners, timers, actors or RPC paths just because two roots reference the same original mechanism.
families.semanticGuardrail: Keep the original event cardinality and lifecycle; one component owner does not mean one aggregated gameplay effect.
families.smallestExperiment: Count component owners and event callbacks for one full lifecycle, including cleanup and reconnect.

families.label: Replacement carrier forwarding/remap
families.definition: Choose one concrete projectile/object replacement carrier and retarget or forward the other overclock's class-filtered leaves, payloads or numeric fields onto that carrier without changing intended gameplay semantics.
families.inclusionRule: A single replacement slot or class filter would otherwise make one overclock unreachable, but both original effects have a coherent literal union.
families.exclusionRule: A bridge/remap is not a gameplay redesign unless it changes triggers, multiplicity, terminal behavior, cost or effect meaning.
families.semanticGuardrail: Forward each effect exactly once to the actual resolving payload; never copy it to mother and child objects indiscriminately.
families.smallestExperiment: Use one replacement object and verify each original effect fires once at its original trigger and authority boundary.

families.label: Bounded multi-object fan-out
families.definition: Preserve an original, statically bounded bounce, pellet, target or child-object fan-out and apply downstream effects independently to each emitted object or impact.
families.inclusionRule: The object/impact bound is evidenced and the fusion does not add recursion or a new unbounded generator.
families.exclusionRule: Do not replace N independent impacts or impulses with one N-scaled aggregate operation.
families.semanticGuardrail: No normalization, arbitrary cap or trigger collapse; preserve per-object state and ordering.
families.smallestExperiment: Count emitted objects/impacts and downstream effect calls; the observed counts must match the evidenced bound.

families.label: Shared input/state/dispatch conflict
families.definition: Two original mechanisms touch the same input phase, state slot, targeting meaning or dispatch component, so native coexistence and ordering must be discriminated before choosing a bridge or redesign.
families.inclusionRule: One effect can become swallowed, redundant, repeatedly toggled or unreachable even though the asset leaf types differ.
families.exclusionRule: Do not pre-emptively add a state machine or new gameplay rule before the smallest native-union experiment fails.
families.semanticGuardrail: Preserve press/release timing, state duration, target selection and one-shot guards; never resolve ambiguity by silently dropping one overclock.
families.smallestExperiment: Exercise the exact input/state sequence with counters that show which branch ran and in what order.

families.label: Performance-sensitive multiplicity
families.definition: Use original or bridged semantics whose valid object/event count can materially increase with fire rate, lifetime, path samples or parent-child multiplicity and therefore needs measurement.
families.inclusionRule: The pair changes concurrent object/event scale without already requiring new gameplay semantics.
families.exclusionRule: Potential cost alone does not authorize caps, pooling, merged damage/force, reduced trigger frequency or normalization.
families.semanticGuardrail: First measure real counts and frame/network cost; any later limit is a separate human-facing tradeoff.
families.smallestExperiment: Record peak live objects, spawn/event rate and cleanup under a representative worst valid use, without a cap.

families.label: Pair-specific gameplay redesign
families.definition: Implement a pair-specific rule because the desired result changes original trigger timing, multiplicity, terminal behavior, cost, reachability or effect meaning rather than merely carrying both original effects.
families.inclusionRule: The gameplay rule is explicitly human-approved or the original mechanisms are semantically incompatible and need a human choice.
families.exclusionRule: A new class, bridge, remap or component is not sufficient evidence of redesign by itself.
families.semanticGuardrail: Preserve the exact approved rule; do not add safety caps, compensation or old AI constants that were not approved.
families.smallestExperiment: Test this pair alone with exact trigger/object/effect counters and host/client authority evidence.

families.label: Verified construction transaction reference
families.definition: Existing reference rows that validate only construction-time registration and the protected preset rebuild/restore transaction within their recorded scope.
families.inclusionRule: The formal row is one of the four verified framework references.
families.exclusionRule: Framework validation does not prove other weapons, carriers, arithmetic or gameplay behavior.
families.semanticGuardrail: Do not use reference status to claim an untested pair or global family is gameplay-confirmed.
families.smallestExperiment: No new experiment for the recorded reference scope; every new family still needs its own representative.
